title: bug: a launch outage carried into a verified-local iteration never ends: the VM route turns every launch probe into a no-launch while the outage suppresses every claim (moe-agent.sh)
description:
Found while planning task-1ccae85c. It is the residual of QA hand-forward comment-87cd53fd (b) on CQ-M07m (task-828e7d21).

Since M07m, a VM-route iteration never ENTERS a launch outage (scripts/moe-agent.sh:11953 gates outage entry on VM_ROUTE != true). But LAUNCH_OUTAGE is wrapper-process state, and the readiness gate re-reads the profile on every iteration.

Repro:
1. A legacy-profile bash worker seat reaches 3 fast launch failures, so LAUNCH_OUTAGE=true and the held task is released.
2. The project flips to verified-local (ready) while that wrapper process lives.
3. On the next iteration VM_ROUTE=true and the seat VM starts. The claim is suppressed (~:10022, outage with nothing held).
4. The taskless decision sets LAUNCH_PROBE=true and prints `MOE_LAUNCH_PROBE ... launching a taskless launch probe` (~:11037). The VM block then turns that probe into a no-launch (`reason=vm-route`).
5. MOE_SKIP_LAUNCH leaves the streak and the outage as they were (~:11923). Only a launch that runs clears the outage (~:11985), so the seat never claims again. It idles until a hot reload or relaunch resets the shell state.

Fix direction (the planner decides): a VM-route iteration does not honour a carried-over outage, because outage mode is a host-CLI concept and the VM route has its own job-failure budget. Either clear the outage state when the route engages, or skip the outage claim-suppression and the probe on the route. Also, print MOE_LAUNCH_PROBE only when a probe actually launches. Legacy launches and outage handling must stay byte-identical.

Test needs a mid-run readiness flip. The shared fixture scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js answers FAKE_READINESS from env only, so it needs an additive knob that is inert when unset. The PowerShell twin follows CQ-M07n (task-62ec51f1), which mirrors M07m's outage exemption.
definitionOfDone: A bash verified-local iteration that starts in a launch outage carried over from a legacy iteration claims again, launches no host CLI, and prints no MOE_LAUNCH_PROBE line.
Legacy launch-outage behavior and diagnostics are byte-identical; the existing postflight.sh launch-outage rows pass unchanged.
A postflight-vm-route.sh row flips readiness mid-run (legacy outage, then verified-local) and asserts the claim resumes; focused wrapper rows and parity-check pass.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 1, 2. scripts/moe-agent.sh: a VM-route iteration ends a launch outage carried over from a legacy iteration. Add ONE guarded block immediately after the per-iteration gate call `case "$ROLE" in worker|qa) verified_local_gate ;; esac` (~:9959), before `if [ "$AUTO_CLAIM" = true ]`:

```bash
if [ "$VM_ROUTE" = true ] && [ "$LAUNCH_OUTAGE" = true ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}[launch-outage]${NC} The verified-local VM route runs this seat's sessions in its VM, never the host CLI: launch outage over, claiming resumes."
    if [ -n "${GENERAL_CHANNEL_ID:-}" ]; then
        LAUNCH_OK_MSG="$WORKER_ID: the verified-local VM route runs this seat's sessions in its VM, never the host CLI, after $LAUNCH_FAIL_STREAK host launch failures. Launch outage over: claiming resumes."
        LAUNCH_OK_ARGS=<the same python json.dumps line the success branch uses, ~:11981>
        moe_rpc chat_send "$LAUNCH_OK_ARGS" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
    fi
    LAUNCH_FAIL_STREAK=0; LAUNCH_FAIL_BACKOFF_SEC=0
    LAUNCH_OUTAGE=false; LAUNCH_OUTAGE_HELD_TASK_ID=""; LAUNCH_OUTAGE_RELEASE_TRIED=""; LAUNCH_OUTAGE_ANNOUNCE=false
fi
```

The six resets are exactly the success branch's (~:11987-11992). Put a 3-4 line comment above it: outage mode is host-CLI state; the VM route never enters it (the fast-failure branch gates entry on VM_ROUTE != true, ~:11961) and turns a probe into a no-launch, so an outage carried over from a legacy iteration of this wrapper process would suppress every claim forever (task-cc4213c0); the route's own job failures restart the shared streak/backoff from 0.

Why here: VM_ROUTE is reset to false at every iteration start (~:9904) and set true only inside verified_local_gate after every refusal check, so the block runs only on an engaged route. Everything that reads the outage later in the iteration then sees none: the claim suppression (~:10022), the claim-wait gate (~:10115), the pre-flight outage branches (~:10437-10461), the probe decision (~:11037) and launch_outage_postflight (~:12398). Do NOT edit any of those sites. The MOE_LAUNCH_PROBE echo becomes unreachable on the route, so it prints only before a probe that really launches (the description's second ask). Legacy output keeps its exact text and order.

A held outage task (a refused release, or BLOCKED) is covered too. The marked claim answers alreadyAssigned and the route resumes it; launch_outage_postflight never releases a VM seat's task.

No new MOE_* token, so the parity families are unchanged. moe-agent.ps1 is untouched: its twin goes with CQ-M07n (task-62ec51f1).

Error handling: the chat post is best-effort (`|| true`) and never blocks the iteration, and an empty GENERAL_CHANNEL_ID skips it. GENERAL_CHANNEL_ID still holds the previous iteration's join value here; the reset at ~:9972 comes later.

Edit in place in the task worktree with the Edit tool, then run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh`. Never temp+mv (scripts/CLAUDE.md, worktree mode). The new test row comes in step 3.
implementationPlan.note: Added the guarded VM_ROUTE && LAUNCH_OUTAGE block right after the verified_local_gate call site: one [launch-outage] line, a best-effort #general chat_send (same json.dumps pattern as the success branch), and the success branch's six resets. No other site edited. bash -n OK.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 3 (fixture). scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js: an additive knob, inert when unset, inside the readiness handler only. Place it immediately ABOVE `if (tool === 'get_execution_readiness' && process.env.FAKE_READINESS) {` (~:454):

```js
if (tool === 'get_execution_readiness' && process.env.FAKE_READINESS_AFTER) { ... }
```

Behaviour:
- Parse the value with /^(\d+):([\s\S]+)$/ into <n> and <mode>. A value that does not match throws, so a typo fails the row loudly (the same as the handler's unparseable-JSON throw).
- Every get_execution_readiness call increments .moe/readiness-count: ensureDir, then read, increment, write (the heartbeat-count pattern, ~:365).
- From call n+1 on, set `process.env.FAKE_READINESS = mode`. The existing handler then answers exactly as FAKE_READINESS=<mode> does (JSON, unknown, refuse or fail).
- Calls 1..n keep whatever FAKE_READINESS (or its unset default) gives.

This models a project whose profile flips while a wrapper process lives. The wrapper reads readiness exactly once per iteration, in verified_local_gate (moe-agent.sh ~:9737), so <n> counts iterations.

Document the knob in 2-3 comment lines at the handler only. Do NOT touch the header comment or any other handler. task-e76f32a0 edits this file's get_commit_scope region, and an additive hunk here lets merge-tree land both.

Error handling: a missing or unreadable count file counts as 0, as the other counters do. The knob changes nothing when unset: no readiness-count file is written. The test row that uses it comes in step 3.
implementationPlan.note: FAKE_READINESS_AFTER=<n>:<mode> handler placed immediately above the FAKE_READINESS handler (3 comment lines, header untouched). Counts reads in .moe/readiness-count (missing/unreadable = 0); from read n+1 sets process.env.FAKE_READINESS=mode. Spot-checked: 2:<json> answers default, default, json; unset writes nothing under the project; a malformed value throws (exit 1).

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 1, 3 (test). scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.sh: add row VR-outage in the `[seat job]` subshell, after the three VR-taskless rows and before `echo '[seat job] VR-reload…'`.

Setup:
- A fake host CLI at "$TMP_DIR/outage-bin/outage-cli". Its basename is not codex/gemini/grok, so CLI_TYPE stays claude (moe-agent.sh ~:631). It appends `{"tool":"host-cli","args":{}}` to "$FAKE_CALL_LOG" (inherited through vmr_run), so the call log orders it among the RPCs, and it exits 1 at once.
- `VMR_ARGS=(--poll-interval 0)`: single-shot without --no-loop. A launch failure relaunches after its backoff, and the first iteration that neither fails nor probes ends the run (loop end ~:12405).
- `VMR_CMD="$TMP_DIR/outage-bin/outage-cli"`.
- `vmr_run VR-outage worker claude "$LEGACY" on 0 FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=idle FAKE_MENTION=1 FAKE_READINESS_AFTER="3:$READY" MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION=off MOE_LAUNCH_BACKOFF_BASE_SEC=1 MOE_LAUNCH_BACKOFF_MAX_SEC=1`.

How the run goes:
- Iterations 1-3 read legacy. The fake re-serves its routed mention on every chat_read, so each iteration launches the notification-only host CLI. It fails fast every time, and the third failure enters the outage with no task held.
- Iteration 4 reads verified-local ready, starts the seat VM, and (fixed) claims marked. The idle claim then takes the vm-route taskless skip with no seat job, so it needs no VM credential.
- MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION=off is REQUIRED. The block exports rotation on, and under rotation a failed claude run relaunches on the next account and zeroes the streak (the ACCOUNT_RELAUNCH branch, ~:11935), so the outage would never be entered.

Assertions: a node heredoc over "$CALLS", "$OUT" (ANSI stripped), "$PROJECT/.moe/evidence-rpcs.jsonl" and "$PROJECT/.moe/messages/chan-general.jsonl"; any failure goes to vmr_fail VR-outage.
- Exit 0.
- 'entering launch outage mode' appears: the carried-over precondition.
- The step-1 local line appears exactly once.
- No 'MOE_LAUNCH_PROBE' anywhere.
- Exactly 3 host-cli rows, all before the 4th get_execution_readiness.
- At least one claim_next_task before the flip, each with no executionRoute key.
- At least one claim_next_task after the flip, each with executionRoute 'vm'. This is the resumed claim.
- The agent-seat cmds are exactly ['seat-start','seat-stop'].
- The chat file has 'after 3 host launch failures. Launch outage over: claiming resumes.'.
- Then `vmr_one_reason VR-outage vm-route`.

Afterwards, restore `VMR_ARGS=(--no-loop --poll-interval 0)` (VMR_CMD resets itself) and add 'outage' to the block's PASS echo line. Iterate with `bash scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.sh` alone (~1-2 min). Error handling: every assertion names what it expected, and vmr_fail dumps the wrapper output.
implementationPlan.note: Row VR-outage added in the [seat job] block before VR-reload: fake host CLI outage-bin/outage-cli (logs host-cli into $CALLS, baked path; exits 1), VMR_ARGS=(--poll-interval 0), FAKE_READINESS_AFTER=3:$READY, rotation off, backoff 1/1. Node assertions: exit 0, outage entered, one outage-over line (the VM-route text), no MOE_LAUNCH_PROBE, 3 host-cli rows all before the 4th readiness read, unmarked legacy claims before / vm-marked claims after the flip, seats [seat-start, seat-stop], #general 'after 3 host launch failures. Launch outage over: claiming resumes.'; then vmr_one_reason vm-route. VMR_ARGS restored; PASS line gains 'outage'. env -i Node 24 run of postflight-vm-route.sh alone: PASS, rc=0 (3m56s).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Two fixes were weighed: (1) clear the outage when the route engages, or (2) skip the outage claim-suppression and the probe on the route at each read site. (2) touches 3-5 legacy-adjacent sites (~:10022, ~:10115, ~:11037, ~:12398) and leaves stale LAUNCH_OUTAGE/streak state that a VM job failure or a profile flip-back would misread. (1) is one guarded block at the gate call site, so legacy bytes stay byte-identical.

The outage clear also posts a #general line. The outage entry told governors 'this seat claims no new task until a launch probe succeeds', and the legacy success branch posts the matching 'Launch outage over: claiming resumes.'

Test designs:
- A task-holding legacy outage was rejected for the row. A claude VM seat job needs account rotation ON (vm-credential needs ACCOUNT_LEASED_ID), while rotation turns failed legacy launches into account relaunches that zero the streak.
- The taskless mention design (FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=idle + FAKE_MENTION=1, rotation off) is deterministic and proves the exact mechanics: the claim suppression and the probe turned into a no-launch.
- The readiness flip is a count knob, not a marker file. Readiness is read exactly once per iteration.

The docs (TROUBLESHOOTING.md:427-431, 'the first launch that runs ends the outage') are deferred to the CQ-M07 final docs sweep. verified-local is not activatable yet, and the VM route is undocumented by design.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
moe-agent.sh flow per iteration: :9904 resets VM_ROUTE=false. :9959 runs verified_local_gate, which sets VM_ROUTE=true only after the WSL, CLI, worktree, ready, auto-claim and codex-key checks, then starts the seat VM. Then come the pre-flight join (:9972 resets GENERAL_CHANNEL_ID), the claim (:10022, suppressed in an outage with nothing held), the claim-wait (:10115, skipped in an outage or with an unread mention), the taskless decision (:11033-11047: the probe echo, then the VM block turning any taskless iteration into a no-launch) and the launch classification (:11928 skip, :11935 account relaunch, :11944 fast failure with outage entry gated on VM_ROUTE != true at :11961, :11976 success clears the outage). Post-flight follows, then launch_outage_postflight (:12398), and the loop end (:12405): single-shot keeps going only after a failed launch or a probe.

CLI_TYPE defaults to claude for any basename except codex/gemini/grok (:631). The fake proxy logs every claim into evidence-rpcs.jsonl, and FAKE_CALL_LOG has the full call order. The fake re-serves FAKE_MENTION=1 on every chat_read (stateless).
planningNotes.risks:
- Under rotation, a failed claude run never builds a streak; the row must pass MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION=off.
- The flip count assumes one readiness read per iteration. If a future change adds a read, the row's count shifts; the assertion on 3 host-cli rows before the 4th readiness read catches that.
- The full postflight.sh takes ~30-35 min. Run it detached and poll, and kill only your own recorded PID.
- e76f32a0 edits the fake proxy's get_commit_scope region. Keep this hunk additive in the readiness handler.
- ps1 parity: the new lines are sh-only and not in parity-check's required prose. The ps1 twin goes with CQ-M07n (62ec51f1).
- The worktree wrapper is edited in place with the Edit tool, then bash -n (no atomic temp+mv).
